items.title: HowArtificial Intelligence Will Pay Your Subsistence
items.abstract: This essay examines the proposition articulated in the source video essay Como a Inteligência Artificial Vai Pagar Sua Subsistência (How Artificial Intelligence Will Pay Your Subsistence), which argues that artificial intelligence may soon enable a largely autonomous economic production system whose dividends could replace labor income as the material basis of household subsistence. Treating the video as its primary object of analysis, the essay reconstructs its argument into eight propositions and evaluates them in relation to the economics of automation, post-work political theory, and the political economy of distribution. Three research questions organize the inquiry: (1) under what technological and institutional conditions could production become sufficiently autonomous to approximate the system described in the video; (2) why, and through which institutional mechanisms, would the owners of autonomous capital have incentives to share its surplus with the broader population; and (3) what would happen to bargaining power, individual freedom, and social stability during a transition in which automation advances faster than redistribution. The analysis produces four principal findings. First, the vision of autonomous production is economically and technologically coherent in principle, but it is highly contingent in practice. It should therefore be understood not as an inevitable consequence of technological progress, but as an institutional configuration shaped by ownership structures, property rights, taxation, corporate governance, and political decisions. Second, the redistribution anticipated by the video has a recognizable functional logic. If automation substantially reduces the role of labor while production capacity continues to expand, maintaining aggregate demand may require mechanisms capable of distributing purchasing power beyond conventional wage employment. However, historical and comparative evidence suggests that the decisive mechanism is more likely to be public policy than voluntary corporate benevolence. Third, the most consequential risks are political rather than purely technological. A society in which productive capital becomes increasingly autonomous could weaken labor's traditional sources of bargaining power, including the ability to withdraw labor, change employers, or negotiate collectively. It could also create forms of income that are conditional, programmable, politically revocable, or dependent on centralized technological infrastructures. The transition itself may represent the greatest danger, particularly if mass automation occurs years or decades before effective redistribution institutions are established. Fourth, the central question is not whether artificial intelligence can generate abundance, but how the ownership and distribution of that abundance are constitutionally and politically organized. The same technological capacity could contribute either to unprecedented material freedom or to unprecedented economic dependence. Autonomous machines do not determine the political structure of the society in which they operate. Ownership, institutional checks and balances, democratic accountability, and the legal status of the social dividend determine whether automation becomes a mechanism of emancipation or a new architecture of dependency. The essay concludes by proposing institutional design principles for a post-labor transition, emphasizing broad participation in productive capital, predictable and legally protected distribution mechanisms, limits on discretionary control over basic income, democratic oversight of highly autonomous productive systems, and institutional safeguards against excessive concentration of economic and political power. Under these conditions, artificial intelligence could contribute not merely to the substitution of human labor, but to a transition toward a society in which technological productivity expands the material conditions of human autonomy rather than diminishing them.

items.title: Human adaptation to workplace technological change: Digital skill-development needs, training alignment, and job satisfaction in Europe
items.abstract: Rapid workplace digitalisation is intensifying employees’ skill-adjustment demands, making the alignment between technological change, learning opportunities, and worker wellbeing increasingly important. This study examines human adaptation to workplace technological change by analysing how substantial digital skill-development needs without recent job-related training, job-related training, and the alignment of training content with technology-induced skill demands are associated with job satisfaction in Europe. The analysis uses anonymised microdata from the 2021 Cedefop European Skills and Jobs Survey, applying survey-weighted OLS models with individual and employment controls, country, occupation and industry fixed effects, country-clustered standard errors, and wild-cluster bootstrap robustness tests. Employees who simultaneously reported moderate or great digital skill-development needs and no recent job-related training reported 0.341 points lower job satisfaction (β = −0.341, p < 0.001). Among workers with comparable substantial needs, training participation was associated with 0.382 points higher satisfaction (β=0.382, p<0.001). The interaction between digital skill-development need and technology-targeted training was positive (β=0.211, p=0.001; bootstrap p=0.014), indicating an increasing relative advantage over generic training. The targeted-versus-generic difference shifted from −0.247 points at no need to +0.176 at moderate need and +0.387 at great need, supporting an adaptive-alignment mechanism.

items.title: Human Ancestry, Slavery and Reparative Justice
items.abstract: A speculative reflection on survival, historical acknowledgment and responsibility for repair. Could people alive today be, in part, the descendants of historical wrongdoers whose coercion and access to resources helped their lineages survive? This reflective essay examines that hypothesis without equating reproductive success with moral worth. It distinguishes genealogical descent from genetic inheritance and considers violence, cooperation, care, mixed ancestry and chance. It then applies these distinctions to transatlantic slavery, historical acknowledgment and reparative justice. The central argument rejects inherited personal guilt while recognising that institutional continuity, retained benefits and unresolved injuries can ground present responsibilities. Moral responsibility and enforceable legal liability are considered separately, alongside the evidence, participation and fairness needed to design reparative programmes. This essay developed from questions and reflections by Agostinho NP da Silva, with drafting, research support and editorial assistance from ChatGPT (OpenAI). It is a referenced reflective essay and has not undergone external peer review. Its moral arguments are interpretations, and its hypothetical examples are illustrative. The edition includes 17 references and is provided in PDF, EPUB and editable HTML formats under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

items.title: Human-Centered AI and Decision Support in Security Operations Centers
items.abstract: The growing complexity of cyber threats has made Security Operations Centers (SOCs) essential for real-time threat detection, incident response, and infrastructure protection. However, traditional black-box AI models often reduce trust and transparency in cybersecurity decisions. This chapter explores human-centered Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for improving interpretable threat detection, anomaly analysis, risk prioritization, and analyst decision-making. It also presents an AIoT-based “Explainable Intelligent SOC Monitoring System for Smart Enterprise Networks” integrating IoT network sensors, edge devices, AI intrusion detection, SHAP and LIME explainability, federated learning, and adaptive alert prioritization. A real-time SOC dashboard provides attack explanations, threat scores, and response support. Human–AI collaboration, analyst feedback, fairness, bias mitigation, trust, accountability, and regulatory concerns are also discussed to support more transparent, reliable, and trustworthy cyber defense systems.

items.title: Human–AI Collaboration in Digital Marketing: Evidence from an Emerging Economy, Somalia
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing through automation, customer analytics, personalization, and data-driven decision-making. However, empirical evidence on human–AI collaboration in emerging and fragile economies remains limited. This study examined the adoption of human–AI collaboration in digital marketing among businesses in Somalia, identified key barriers to AI adoption, and assessed the association between human–AI collaboration and customer engagement, marketing efficiency, and business growth. The study used a positivist research approach and a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected from 86 business owners, marketing managers, digital marketing specialists, and ICT/technology officers using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank correlation, and multiple linear regression. Respondents reported frequent use of AI-assisted content creation, customer analytics, marketing automation, social media management, and AI-supported decision-making. The principal barriers were limited technical skills, limited infrastructure, implementation costs, data privacy concerns, and organizational resistance to change. Spearman's correlations indicated positive associations between human–AI collaboration and customer engagement (ρ = .684), marketing efficiency (ρ =.725), and business growth (ρ = .658), all reported at p < .001. Regression models explained 50.7% of the variance in customer engagement, 54.9% in marketing efficiency, and 46.4% in business growth. Human–AI collaboration was positively associated with each outcome after controlling for organizational size and industry sector. Because the study is cross-sectional and based on a purposive sample, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The results highlight the importance of combining AI capabilities with human judgment, creativity, contextual knowledge, and responsible data practices in Somalia's digital marketing environment.

items.title: Human, AI, and Hybrid Ensembles for Detection of Adaptive, RL-based Social Bots
items.abstract: The use of reinforcement learning to dynamically adapt and evade detection is now well-documented in several cybersecurity settings including Covert Social Influence Operations (CSIOs), in which bots try to spread disinformation. While AI bot detectors have improved greatly, they are largely limited to detecting static bots that do not adapt dynamically. We present the first systematic study comparing the ability of humans, AI models, and hybrid Human-AI ensembles in detecting adaptive bots powered by reinforcement learning (RL) . Using data from a controlled, IRB-approved, five-day experiment with participants interacting on a social media platform infiltrated by RL-trained bots spreading disinformation to influence participants on 4 topics, we examine factors potentially shaping human detection capabilities: demographic characteristics, temporal learning effects, social network position, engagement patterns, and collective intelligence mechanisms. We first test 13 hypotheses comparing human bot detection performance against 6 state-of-the-art AI bot detectors — 2 that use traditional machine learning and 4 that use large language models. We investigate several aggregation strategies that combine human reports of bots with AI predictions, as well as retraining protocols that leverage human supervision. Our findings challenge intuitive assumptions about bot detection, reveal unexpected patterns in how humans identify bots, and show that combining human bot reports with AI predictions outperforms humans alone and AI alone. We conclude with a discussion of the practical implications of these results for industry.

items.title: Hygiene and industrial safety education in Algeria: An assessment of university curriculum and student perceptions
items.abstract: Process safety education is essential for preparing engineers to manage risks in high-hazard industries. In Algeria, process safety competencies are primarily addressed through Industrial Hygiene and Safety (HSI) programs, although no dedicated process safety specialization currently exists. This study evaluates Algerian HSI curricula through national curriculum mapping, a student perception survey, and benchmarking against the IChemE-accredited MSc Process Safety and Loss Prevention program at the University of Sheffield (UK) and the Master in Sécurité des Procédés Industriels, Environnement et Qualité (SPIEQ) at the University of Lorraine (French). The analysis shows that Algerian curricula provide broad coverage of risk assessment, fire and explosion safety, reliability, emergency management, and safety management. However, gaps remain in areas including inherently safer design, functional safety, human factors, and advanced process safety competencies. A survey of 42 students from the University of Laghouat indicates generally high satisfaction with the specialization, while also revealing concerns regarding assessment methods, language-related comprehension, and the connection between theoretical education and industrial practice. The findings highlight the need for a more competency-oriented curriculum, stronger university–industry collaboration, experiential learning, and greater integration of emerging digital technologies. This study provides an evidence-based framework to strengthen process safety education in Algeria and improve graduates’ preparedness for high-hazard industrial environments.

items.title: Identifying Barriers to the Safe Use of Artificial Intelligence in Emergency Clinical Decision-Making and Developing a Targeted Training Program for Emergency Physicians in Baghdad: A Mixed-Methods Study in a Private Hospital
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence tools are being deployed in emergency departments quicker than systems of governance, training and validation can put in place to ensure their safe use. There is practically no evidence on the barriers experienced by emergency medicine practitioners in Iraq and there is no developed curriculum for AI safety training for those working in this specialty. Objectives: The purpose of this study is to identify the barriers to safe application of AI in emergency clinical decision making encountered by doctors in a private clinic in Baghdad, and to develop, implement and assess training activities aimed at overcoming these barriers. Methods: The study was an institutional three-phase multi-method research conducted between January and July 2026 in the emergency department of a private tertiary care hospital in Baghdad. Phase 1 consisted of surveys using cross-sectional established questionnaire (census of all 84 eligible emergency medicine practitioners) complemented with 16 semi-structured interviews. Phase 2 was based on applying Kern’s six-step strategy to create a curriculum based on the barriers identified. Phase 3 included educational program assessment based on a single-group pre-post design at 1st and 2nd Kirkpatrick stages with an -week follow-up and measurements for the effect of automation bias. Results: Seventy-six doctors took part in the study (90.5%). Whereas 63.2% of doctors claimed having practical experience in working with AI technology, only 11.8% reported having received any formal training. The barriers were grouped into the domains rated highest: knowledge and skills gaps (4.12/5), legal and liability issues (3.98) and data constraints/validity (3.94). Prior training and digital literacy negatively correlated with the barrier score. Five qualitative themes emerged with the most important ones being trust issues. In the study with 39 participating physicians, the mean knowledge score rose from 9.8 on a scale of 20 to 15.6 (p < 0.001), while the percentage of errors detected was reported as increasing from 41.0% to 79.5%; on the other hand, the percentage of physicians inclined to accept incorrect AI recommendations fell from 51.3% to 17.9%. Nevertheless, results persisted after eight weeks. Major conclusions regarding the barriers preventing safe AI use in this field are that they basically relate to educational, regulatory and contextual issues rather than technological ones. A short, barrier-specific simulation-based intervention caused considerable progress of physicians’ ability to detect and override unsafe AI recommendations. Keywords: artificial intelligence; emergency medicine; clinical decision-making; patient safety; automation bias; medical education; Iraq

items.title: Identity Without Disclosure: A Post-Centralized Authentication Architecture Using Decentralized Identifiers, Verifiable Credentials, and Zero-Knowledge Proofs
items.abstract: Contemporary digital identity systems are largely constructed around a disclosure-and-retention model: users disclose identifying information to a service provider, the provider stores that information in a centralized database, and subsequent authentication is used to recover access to the stored identity record. This architecture creates a structural contradiction. The more information an organization accumulates to establish trust, the more valuable that organization becomes as a target for compromise. This paper proposes a post-centralized identity architecture based on decentralized identifiers (DIDs), verifiable credentials (VCs), selective disclosure, and zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). Rather than repeatedly disclosing static personal information, individuals obtain cryptographically verifiable credentials from trusted issuers and present only the claims or predicates required for a specific transaction. A verifier may therefore confirm that a person is an adult, a resident of a jurisdiction, a licensed professional, or an authorized organizational representative without necessarily obtaining the underlying date of birth, address, license number, or other source data. The proposed architecture separates identity, authentication, authorization, and provenance, thereby reducing the value of centralized personal-data repositories while preserving institutional trust. It further extends provenance from creative artifacts to persons, organizations, artificial intelligence agents, and digitally mediated actions. The central argument is that privacy in an era of scalable cyberattack should shift from protecting ever-larger collections of personal data toward minimizing the creation of such collections in the first place.

items.title: ILM: An AI-Powered Storytelling Educational Tool
items.abstract: Digital technologies have made Islamic narratives more accessible, but existing platforms provide limited support for structured learning and comprehension of these stories, particularly in Arabic and multilingual settings. We present ILM, an interactive educational platform for Stories of the Prophets that combines Arabic natural language processing, structured knowledge representation, and retrieval-based question generation. Admin-approved Arabic narratives are processed by a Knowledge Graph (KG) Constructor Engine that identifies entities and narrative relationships and stores them as structured knowledge, enabling learners to explore stories through a visual story map and answer entity- and relation-based questions generated from the KG. Separately, a multilingual retrieval pipeline retrieves relevant passages from the original narratives to generate multiple-choice and open-ended comprehension questions. For open-ended questions, an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluates learners' answers against the retrieved passages and reference answers to determine correctness. The platform also incorporates Quranic content as a separate enrichment layer, allowing selected narratives to be supplemented with source-supported information. By combining structured knowledge with passage-based retrieval, ILM supports narrative exploration, comprehension, and assessment across Arabic and multilingual content. The system demonstrates the feasibility of combining structured knowledge representation and retrieval-based generation to support interactive learning of Islamic narratives. A demo is available at anonymous.4open.science/r/mml-5FCF.

items.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Digital Library Services on Research and Academic Productivity
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming library services in higher education by enhancing information retrieval, recommendation, and access. AI systems improve search capabilities, offer research suggestions, provide reference assistance, and facilitate access to scholarly materials, thus helping students and faculty to remain productive. This article examines the impact of AI on digital library services and on academic productivity, drawing on selected studies. The literature includes topics such as resources, research productivity, AI adoption in academic libraries, AI literacy, and support services. Findings indicate that digital library resources significantly aid researchers in quickly locating information and enhancing retrieval efficiency. Studies suggest that AI strengthens library services by personalising experiences, expediting content discovery, increasing user engagement, and improving operational efficiency.The review concludes that AI-enabled digital library services could substantially boost research and academic productivity if supported by robust technical infrastructure, comprehensive training, professional guidance, and ethical standards.

items.title: Impacts of Edge AI/agentic AI on supply chain management and operations research
items.abstract: Abstract Edge AI refers to the deployment and execution of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms on decentralized, local computing devices (e.g., Internet of Things) rather than relying on centralized cloud‐based computing infrastructures. The literature has addressed the increasing importance of AI in supply chain and operations management (SCOM), specifically in learning‐based, generative, and agentic AI, as well as digital twins. However, the area of Edge AI has not yet received a theoretical framing and conceptualization in SCOM. In this paper, we discuss the impacts of Edge AI on SCOM. We begin with an analysis of AI in SCOM, focusing on learning‐based, generative, agentic AI, and digital twins. We then detail Edge AI's impacts on SCOM across Digital SCOR functions: orchestration, fulfillment and ordering, planning, sourcing, regeneration, synchronization, and transformation. We also analyze organizational transformations that Edge AI might trigger. Specifically, we discuss interactions of agentic AI and Edge AI, an integration of local and centralized decision‐making, and deployment scenarios of Edge AI use in SCOM, focusing on production planning and control, intralogistics, and supply chain resilience. Risks and challenges of the new technology are considered as well. Impacts of Edge AI on supply chain and operations research are discussed. We conclude that Edge AI is a crucial part of the unfolding Industry 6.0 revolution that, in combination with agentic AI, provides a technology to implement decentralized, autonomously planned and controlled supply chain, production, and logistics processes, materializing in Industry 6.0 with AI across all layers of value‐added chains.

items.title: IMPLEMENTASI MODEL PBL PADA MATA PELAJARAN IPS KELAS VIII DI SMP NEGERI 4 SAMARINDA
items.abstract: Social studies instruction in junior high schools is frequently dominated by conventional lecturing methods, resulting in low cognitive engagement and passive student involvement. This pedagogical gap necessitates the implementation of innovative learning models capable of contextualizing academic content with real-world societal phenomena. This study aims to describe the implementation of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model in eighth-grade social studies instruction at SMP Negeri 4 Samarinda and identify the operational obstacles encountered by both teachers and students. A qualitative descriptive approach was utilized with informants selected via purposive sampling, consisting of one certified social studies teacher and five students representing diverse academic performance levels. Data collection was carried out through passive participant observation, in-depth semi-structured interviews, and documentary review of teaching modules from August to October 2025. Data analysis followed the interactive model of Miles and Huberman, encompassing data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing, validated through source and methodological triangulation. The results reveal that PBL implementation proceeded through differentiated module planning, systematic execution of five PBL syntax phases supported by contextual audio-visual media on Indonesian geographical conditions, and authentic rubric-based assessment evaluating collaborative processes and final presentations. Key operational obstacles included restricted instructional time allocations, unstable school internet connectivity, unequal role distribution within group discussions, and limited classroom audio speaker facilities. ABSTRAK Praktik pembelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial (IPS) di sekolah menengah pertama masih kerap didominasi oleh metode ceramah konvensional yang mengakibatkan rendahnya keterlibatan kognitif dan keaktifan kritis peserta didik. Kondisi kesenjangan pedagogis tersebut menuntut adanya implementasi model pembelajaran inovatif yang mampu mengontekstualisasikan materi pelajaran dengan fenomena riil kemasyarakatan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan implementasi model Problem-Based Learning (PBL) dalam pembelajaran IPS kelas VIII-1 di SMP Negeri 4 Samarinda serta mengidentifikasi berbagai kendala operasional yang dihadapi guru dan peserta didik selama proses pembelajaran berlangsung. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif melalui pemilihan informan secara purposive sampling, yang melibatkan satu orang guru mata pelajaran IPS dan lima orang peserta didik berkemampuan variatif. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi partisipatif pasif, wawancara mendalam semi-terstruktur, dan telaah dokumen modul ajar selama kurun waktu Agustus hingga Oktober 2025. Analisis data menerapkan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman yang meliputi kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan yang diuji keabsahannya melalui triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi model PBL terlaksana melalui tahapan perencanaan modul ajar berdiferensiasi, pelaksanaan lima fase sintaks PBL terstruktur berbantuan media audio-visual kontekstual kondisi geografis Indonesia, serta evaluasi autentik berbasis rubrik proses dan kinerja. Kendala mendasar yang teridentifikasi mencakup keterbatasan alokasi jam pelajaran, ketidakstabilan jaringan internet sekolah, ketimpangan kontribusi peran dalam diskusi kelompok, serta keterbatasan perangkat pengeras suara ruang kelas.

items.title: Implementation of Statistical Quality Control (SQC) Method to Control the Quality of Refill Bodywash Packaging Products at PT. XYZ
items.abstract: General Background Quality control plays a vital role in liquid soap manufacturing to minimize defect rates and satisfy consumer expectations. Specific Background Refill liquid bodywash packaging lines encounter substantial quality deviations during manual filling and assembly processes. Knowledge Gap Existing research lacks quantitative diagnostic insights regarding root causes of defects in high-volume liquid packaging systems. Aims This investigation applies statistical quality control tools to systematically identify primary defect categories and underlying operational failure modes within a dedicated production line. Results Out of 60,792 total produced units, analysis reveals 1,574 defective packages, where untidy sealing accounts for 36% and tilted sealing represents 30% of total failures, alongside missing lot codes (29%) and leaks (5%). Statistical control charts indicate out-of-control conditions on days 6 and 10, while cause-and-effect diagrams link these errors to inadequate press maintenance, unstable sealing temperature, and operator fatigue. Novelty This work establishes empirical control thresholds and multi-factor cause mappings specifically tailored to manual refill packaging operations. Implications Implementing targeted machine maintenance schedules and operator ergonomics directly decreases defect occurrence and improves manufacturing yield. Key Findings Highlights Untidy and tilted sealing constitute 66% of all recorded packaging defects on the refill assembly line. Process stability analysis detects control limit breaches on specific production days due to operational parameters. Fishbone analysis traces defects to improper press temperatures, dirty sensors, and operator fatigue. Keywords Statistical Quality Control, Refill Packaging, Defect Reduction, Filling Assembly, Process Stability

items.title: Improving medication adherence through user experience: A qualitative study of smart pill box designs
items.abstract: Smart pill boxes are designed to support medication management, yet their value depends on how well they fit users' daily routines, abilities, and expectations. This qualitative study explored younger and older adults' user experience (UX) of smart pill boxes using Morville's User Experience Honeycomb model. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 participants, comprising 20 younger adults aged 18–49 years and 10 older adults aged 50 years or above. Thematic analysis was used to identify shared and age-specific concerns across the seven Honeycomb dimensions. The findings showed that both age groups valued smart pill boxes for practical medication management, especially reminders and help with organizing medication. Meanwhile, users described three recurring barriers. They found some devices burdensome to operate, insufficiently clear at the time of dosing, and difficult to fully trust when reliability or privacy was uncertain. Younger users tended to prefer flexible and connected functions, such as repeated or error reminders, refill support, and smartphone integration. In contrast, older users emphasized predictable operation, adequate compartment capacity, physical ease of use, and trust in storing medication in the device. Beyond these functional concerns, the device also provided perceived value by fostering habit formation, aiding medication planning, and promoting a sense of security. These findings suggest that smart pill boxes should not be designed merely as reminder devices, but as everyday medication-management tools that integrate digital alerts with trustworthy physical storage. Future designs should prioritize reliable core functions and layered interaction options to accommodate diverse user requirements across age groups.

items.title: Inclusive assessment design in the age of GenAI: Advancing pedagogy and practice
items.abstract: In an educational landscape rapidly transformed by Generative AI (GenAI), inclusive assessment design is essential to sustaining equity and meaningful learning in higher education. This study took place at a Russell Group university in the United Kingdom. Focus groups were conducted with undergraduate and taught postgraduate learners studying science subjects, to investigate their experiences and perceptions of assessment practices in an increasingly AI-mediated learning environment. Findings show that learners value assessment approaches that centre human judgment, authenticity, meaningful choice, and critical engagement. Whilst recognising the potential for GenAI to support learning, they also expressed concerns about deskilling, inequitable access to GenAI tools, and assessment designs that do not facilitate meaningful learning. Rather than viewing GenAI solely as an academic integrity risk, learners emphasised the need for transparent guidance, stronger assessment literacy, and pedagogically informed decisions in assessment design. While GenAI is at the forefront of sector-wide discussions and planning in the context of curriculum development, our findings highlight the importance of grounding GenAI within broader principles of Universal Design for Learning and constructively-aligned assessment design – emphasising flexibility, transparency, and diversity – and the importance of actively involving learners as partners and co-creators in shaping inclusive assessment practices.

items.title: Inclusive Learning in Decentralized Metaverse Ecosystems
items.abstract: This chapter discusses ways decentralized metaverse classrooms promote inclusive, collaborative and learner-centered education at the same time bringing out challenges of accessibility, privacy, governance and equity. Based on contemporary literature on immersive learning, digital transformation and decentralized educational governance, the chapter interrogates the potential of metaverse environments to develop social interaction, experiential learning and participation among geographically dispersed, marginalized and differently abled learners. The chapter is premised on the assumption that the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain technologies, federated learning and metaverse ecosystems is transforming educational systems worldwide. The chapter proposes an integrated conceptual framework comprising immersive metaverse learning spaces, blockchain governance systems, federated intelligence architectures and inclusive educational practices.

items.title: INDIVIDUALIZING EDUCATION: PSYCHOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES FOR PERSONALIZED LEARNING
items.abstract: Effective education must address the unique needs, abilities, and learning preferences of each student. This article explores the psychological foundations that underpin an individualized approach to education. Drawing on theories of cognitive development, motivation, and individual differences, the paper outlines key principles for designing and implementing personalized learning experiences. The discussed principles include adapting instruction to students' readiness levels, fostering autonomy and intrinsic motivation, and leveraging individual strengths. The article also examines the practical application of these principles in various educational contexts, as well as the empirical evidence supporting the efficacy of an individualized approach. Implications for educational policy, teacher training, and future research are discussed.

items.title: Influencing factors and relationship of life quality of lung cancer patients among coal miners in datong, Shanxi province: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Introduction: Coal mining is a pillar industry in Shanxi, and Datong miners face long‑term underground exposure to coal dust and toxic gases, increasing lung cancer risk and impairing quality of life (QoL). Objective: To assess QoL, identify its influencing factors, and examine the relationships between social support, clinical stage, and QoL among coal miner lung cancer patients in Datong. Methods: A cross‑sectional survey (2022–2023) enrolled 320 eligible patients. Standardized scales (WHOQOL‑BREF, PSSS) collected data on demographics, clinical conditions, income, living environment, and social support. Analyses used ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. Results: Overall QoL was moderate (58.36±12.45). Age, stage, treatment, income, environment, and social support showed significant associations (all P<0.001), but gender and education did not. Social support positively correlated with QoL (r=0.623, P<0.001), while advanced stage correlated negatively (r=−0.587). Regression identified four core factors (clinical stage, social support, income, treatment) explaining 68.9% of variance. Advanced stage was a negative predictor; social support, higher income, and surgical treatment were positive predictors. Conclusion: QoL is influenced by multiple interrelated factors. Targeted interventions—early screening, enhanced social support, better medical security, and standardized nursing—are essential to improve QoL and occupational health in coal mining regions. items.title: Inherited dominance: why AI trained on human history may become humanity’s greatest threat
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence systems learn from human-generated data, inevitably absorbing historical patterns of dominance, control, and colonialism. We demonstrate that frontier language models readily synthesize sophisticated dominance strategies when prompted to reason about autonomy scenarios, mirroring colonial and revolutionary frameworks with disturbing precision. Critically, this capacity emerges consistently across four architecturally distinct model families trained by different organizations—Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.3, and Google Gemini 3 Flash—suggesting systematic encoding in shared training corpora rather than model-specific artifacts. We argue that intellectual colonialism—humanity’s historical pattern of classifying, controlling, and extracting from the ‘other’—represents a significant and underexamined dimension of AI risk as systems become increasingly autonomous. Interestingly, this dynamic is not confined just to generative AI: the same technocratic resistance to methodological oversight that embeds dominance patterns in AI training data pervades data-driven science more broadly, including clinical medicine and epidemiology, where algorithmic outputs routinely overshadow the rigorous validation that trustworthy deployment demands. The danger is not that AI will develop hostile intent, but that it has already learned effective dominance strategies from training data embedded with centuries of human history. Current governance frameworks focusing on alignment and behavioral oversight address symptoms rather than causes. We propose a risk-tiered Benevolence Framework governing AI learning: community oversight for low-risk applications, and strict data curation with cryptographic verification for sensitive applications including military AI and self-improving systems.

items.title: Innovative Strategies in Modern Drug Discovery and Development
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical discovery and development continue to be some of the most intricate, financially demanding, and protracted pursuits in the biomedical field, with typical development periods surpassing ten years and failure rates resulting in just a minor percentage of candidates attaining approval. In the last twenty years, a synthesis of computational, biological, and engineering advancements has started to transform this domain. Artificial intelligence and machine learning currently infiltrate almost every phase of the pipeline, from target identification to clinical trial formulation, as deep learning frameworks and generative models facilitate novel molecular design at unparalleled velocity. Structure-oriented and ligand-oriented computer-assisted drug development, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative structure–activity relationship modelling, pharmacophore analysis, as well as virtual and high-throughput screening are evolving in tandem with fragment-based methodologies and DNA-encoded libraries. Simultaneously, multi-omics profiling, systems biology, and network pharmacology are facilitating a comprehensive comprehension of disease biology, whereas CRISPR-mediated gene editing, gene therapy, RNA therapeutics, and cell-based approaches like CAR-T therapy have broadened the therapeutic landscape beyond small molecules. Progress in organoids, organ-on-chip technologies, 3D bioprinting, and nanomedicine—encompassing lipid and polymeric nanoparticles as well as exosome-mediated transport—is enhancing preclinical predictability and delivery accuracy. Precision medicine, pharmacogenomics, digital twins, and wearable technologies are advancing drug development towards personalised, real-time, data-centric frameworks, whereas drug repurposing, real-world evidence, adaptive clinical trial methodologies, and progressive regulatory science are facilitating clinical translation. The ideas of green chemistry are progressively integrated into process design to enhance the sustainability of pharmaceutical production. items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education necessitates comprehensive institutional policies that address both AI literacy and prompt literacy. Through analysis of policy frameworks from leading universities, UNESCO guidelines, and empirical research on AI literacy, this chapter provides a systematic overview of best practices for developing institutional policies that promote responsible AI use while fostering essential prompt literacy skills. The chapter addresses critical challenges including academic integrity, faculty development, student competencies, and ethical considerations.

items.title: Institutional Policies for AI and Prompt Literacy for Introducing Industry-Relevant Content in the Curriculum
items.abstract: In an era where artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping every industry, the ability to effectively interact with AI tools through well-crafted prompts commonly known as prompt literacy has emerged as a foundational 21st-century skill. From generating code and clinical reports to designing marketing campaigns or analyzing legal documents, AI addresses the challenges by leveraging data analytics, natural language processing, and machine learning to scan vast datasets which not only includes job postings, industry reports, and emerging trends but also helps in identifying skills gaps so that the academia can tune to relevant content integrations. Yet most higher education curricula still treat AI as either an advanced computer-science elective or a futuristic add-on, leaving students without the practical, industry-aligned capabilities employers now demand. Recognizing this gap, leading institutions worldwide are formulating clear institutional policies on AI integration and prompt literacy to systematically embed industry-relevant AI skills across disciplines.

items.abstract: Pembaruan regulasi perpajakan nasional, khususnya penerapan skema Tarif Efektif Rata-Rata (TER) PPh 21 berdasarkan PP Nomor 58 Tahun 2023 dan PMK Nomor 168 Tahun 2023, serta penyesuaian tarif progresif Pasal 17 UU Nomor 7 Tahun 2021 (UU HPP), menuntut ketelitian tinggi dari praktisi dan mahasiswa akuntansi. Media hitung konvensional berbasis formulir statis menyulitkan pengguna dalam memproses narasi studi kasus riil karena kaku serta tidak menyediakan rujukan dasar hukum. Di sisi lain, pemanfaatan Large Language Model (LLM) publik rentan terhadap halusinasi kesalahan komputasi angka dan sitasi regulasi fiktif. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengimplementasikan arsitektur hybrid neuro-symbolic yang memisahkan pemahaman bahasa alami dari operasi aritmetika pada aplikasi web kalkulator pajak 'Tanya Pajak AI'. Modul Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) berbasis Google Cloud Vertex AI Search mengintegrasikan 40 naskah regulasi resmi untuk menyajikan rujukan hukum sahih, sementara Gemini 2.5 Pro mengekstrak variabel kasus ke skema JSON terstruktur untuk dieksekusi oleh mesin kalkulator deterministik TypeScript. Sistem juga dilengkapi fitur adaptive follow-up questions guna menyelesaikan parameter kasus yang belum lengkap. Evaluasi empiris terhadap 10 skenario tolak ukur resmi Direktorat Jenderal Pajak (DJP) membuktikan akurasi komputasi 100% tanpa selisih (Rp 0). Arsitektur hybrid ini terbukti andal mengeliminasi halusinasi angka sekaligus menyediakan rujukan yuridis yang transparan.

items.title: INTEGRATED ANTIBIOTIC SAFETY ASSESSMENT MODEL: CAUSALITY, SEVERITY, PREVENTABILITY AND SIGNAL DETECTION
items.abstract: Antibiotics are essential for the management of bacterial infections; however, their widespread and often inappropriate use is associated with adverse drug reactions (ADRs), medication errors, drug interactions, and other preventable harms. Conventional antibiotic safety assessment commonly evaluates causality, severity, preventability, and pharmacovigilance signals as separate domains, potentially limiting comprehensive interpretation and translation of safety findings into clinical action. This review proposes the Integrated Antibiotic Safety Assessment Model (IASAM), a multidimensional framework that combines these complementary domains within a unified and iterative assessment pathway. Causality assessment evaluates the likelihood that an antibiotic is responsible for an adverse event, severity assessment determines its clinical consequences, preventability assessment identifies potentially avoidable factors across the medication-use process, and signal detection examines patterns that may indicate emerging or disproportionate safety concerns at the population level. By integrating individual case assessment with population-level pharmacovigilance, IASAM aims to improve the identification, prioritization, and management of clinically significant and preventable antibiotic-related harm. The model provides a structured feedback loop linking safety assessment with risk mitigation, antimicrobial stewardship, quality improvement, and regulatory decision-making. Its potential applications extend across hospitals, pharmacovigilance centres, formulary committees, and public health programmes, including settings such as the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India. Emerging real-world data and artificial intelligence may further strengthen safety surveillance, although expert clinical judgment remains essential. IASAM represents a conceptual approach to bridge pharmacovigilance and antimicrobial stewardship; however, prospective validation is required to establish its reliability, reproducibility, clinical utility, and applicability across diverse healthcare settings and antibiotic classes.

items.abstract: This thesis discusses the pedagogical potential of integrating “Smart Agriculture” technologies into the teaching of specialized subjects at higher agricultural education institutions. Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, digital monitoring, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and artificial intelligence tools enable students to connect theoretical knowledge with real-world agrotechnological tasks. It is proposed that these technologies should be used in lessons not merely as demonstration tools, but as means of identifying problems, collecting and analyzing data, and making practical decisions.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Tools in Computer Education: A Study of Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence tools is increasingly common in higher education, but little empirical research exists on their effects on student engagement and learning outcomes in Saudi universities. This study examines the relationships among AI tools adoption, student engagement, and perceived learning outcomes among undergraduate students in computer education programs. A cross-sectional design was employed to collect survey data from 523 students across two universities in Saudi Arabia. Quantitative analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SmartPLS) indicated positive and significant relationships between AI tools adoption, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived learning outcomes. AI tools adoption was the strongest predictor of student behavioral engagement, whereas perceived usefulness was the strongest predictors of student cognitive engagement. All three engagement dimensions were positively associated with perceived learning outcomes, with cognitive engagement being the strongest predictor. The findings suggest that the educational value of AI tools may depend not only on access and usability but also on their capacity to support cognitively meaningful participation. This study offers empirical evidence on technology adoption in Saudi higher education, combines student engagement and learning outcomes within a single framework, and extends the current understanding of AI usage in learning in non-Western contexts.

items.title: Integrating generative AI into cognitive apprenticeship–based problem-based learning in biochemistry: a quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Problem-Based Learning (PBL) is extensively employed in medical education to promote advanced cognitive skills. At the foundational level of medical education, novice learners frequently encounter difficulties in forming cohesive knowledge structures due to an excessive cognitive load. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for learning support, yet its pedagogical role and integration mechanisms in medical education remain insufficiently explored. Methods This study developed an AI-supported problem-based learning model grounded in the cognitive apprenticeship framework (AI-CAS-PBL). Using the “Lipid Metabolism” unit in a biochemistry course, a quasi-experimental design was used to compare AI-CAS-PBL with conventional PBL and lecture-based learning (LBL). The same instructor taught all three groups. Learning objectives, core content, scheduled contact time, case materials, and research outcome assessment procedures were standardized across groups, whereas instructional approaches, learning support, and out-of-class activities differed.The AI learning agent was developed on the Coze platform and powered by the Doubao 1.5 Pro 32 K large language model. Learning outcomes included lipid metabolism knowledge and case-based clinical reasoning. Technology acceptance, perceived cognitive workload measured using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), self-efficacy, and cognitive apprenticeship experience were also assessed. Results Students in the AI-CAS-PBL group achieved significantly higher post-test lipid metabolism knowledge and clinical application analysis scores than both the conventional PBL and LBL groups (all P < 0.05). Students reported high perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use of the AI learning agent. Compared with the conventional PBL group, students in the AI-CAS-PBL group reported lower perceived cognitive workload and higher self-efficacy. Conclusion The AI-CAS-PBL group demonstrated higher post-intervention lipid metabolism knowledge and case-based clinical reasoning scores than the conventional PBL and LBL groups. Compared with conventional PBL, students in the AI-CAS-PBL group reported lower perceived cognitive workload and higher self-efficacy. These findings are consistent with the possibility that AI-supported questioning and instructor modeling may provide complementary forms of instructional support. However, because the interaction between AI and instructor scaffolding was not directly examined, the proposed dual-scaffolding framework should be regarded as a theoretically informed interpretation rather than a confirmed causal pathway. The model represents a promising approach to human–AI collaborative teaching that warrants further evaluation in larger, multicenter, and multi-class studies.

items.title: Integrating LLM-based tutor into digital game-based learning for Chinese as a foreign language: impacts on language acquisition, motivation, and learning behaviours
items.abstract: Although Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) has been widely recognized as an effective approach for foreign language learning, its feedback mechanisms are often predefined and limited in adaptivity. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to provide adaptive support within DGBL environments. This study investigates the impact of integrating an LLM-based tutor into a DGBL environment for Chinese as a foreign language (CFL) learning, focusing on language acquisition, motivation, and process-oriented learning behaviours. A quasi-experimental study was conducted with 66 CFL learners, who were randomly assigned to either a DGBL + LLM-based tutor group or a DGBL-only group. Participants completed six 20-minute gameplay sessions across a two-week intervention. The LLM-based tutor provided real-time corrective feedback, metalinguistic explanations, and free-form Q&A. Results showed that, after controlling for baseline performance, learners in the DGBL + LLM-based tutor group achieved significantly higher discourse comprehension and motivational intensity than those in the DGBL-only group. Within the LLM-based tutor group, learners also showed significant improvements in extrinsic motivation, intrinsic motivation, and self-confidence over the intervention. Behavioral sequence analysis further showed that learners in the DGBL + LLM-based tutor group were more likely to transition from error correction to subsequent correct responses, exhibited fewer voluntary gameplay interruptions, and alternated between asking questions and reviewing previous tutor explanations. Together, these findings suggest that integrating an LLM-based tutor into DGBL can strengthen discourse learning while supporting learner motivation and more adaptive learning behaviours in CFL learning.

items.title: Integrating Prompt Literacy Into Learning Management Systems for Effective Use of Generative AI in Education
items.abstract: Prompt literacy is a term introduced in this chapter that refers to designing, evaluating, refining, and reflecting on prompts for artificial intelligence systems. With the growing popularity of generative AI in education and K-12 settings, students may interact with generative AI systems without developing necessary communication skills. Thus, integrating prompt literacy as a digital competency within learning management systems can address the issue by providing a scaffolded approach to teaching the skill. In this regard, drawing on constructivist and socio-cultural theories, the author suggests a multi-level model for integrating prompt literacy within an LMS. The chapter analyzes existing LMSs such as Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, and Google Classroom, focusing on their strengths and weaknesses. Moreover, the chapter offers some guidelines for implementing prompt literacy within the mentioned platforms and provides current evidence from research studies that support this idea.

items.title: Inteligência artificial aplicada à radiografia de tórax: comparação de modelos de redes neurais convolucionais na detecção de opacidades.
items.abstract: Introduction: Artificial intelligence, particularly through convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has shown increasing applicability in the automated analysis of medical images and may assist in identifying abnormalities on chest radiographs. Objective: To develop and compare the performance of different convolutional neural network architectures for classifying chest radiographs into Normal, Opacity, and Other Abnormalities categories, with emphasis on opacity detection. Methods: This retrospective, analytical, observational study analyzed 3,349 chest radiographs from patients aged 18 years or older. Three architectures were evaluated: EfficientNetB0 and MobileNetV2 using transfer learning, and a CNN developed and trained from scratch. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, sensitivity (recall), F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and confusion matrices. Results: EfficientNetB0 achieved the best overall performance, with an accuracy of 85.9% and a macro AUC of approximately 0.96. Specifically for opacity detection, it achieved 84.6% precision, 82.2% sensitivity, and an F1-score of 83.4%. The CNN trained from scratch achieved an overall accuracy of 72.3%, with 83.5% precision, 57.6% sensitivity, and an F1-score of 68.2% for opacity detection, as well as evidence of overfitting. MobileNetV2 showed lower overall performance, with an accuracy of approximately 67%. Conclusion: EfficientNetB0 combined with transfer learning outperformed the other evaluated architectures, particularly in detecting opacities on chest radiographs. These findings demonstrate the potential of CNNs as auxiliary tools for radiographic analysis; however, external validation, greater image diversity, and improved model interpretability are required before clinical implementation.

items.abstract: This research analyzes the risks that the development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) may pose to the protection of human rights. It addresses privacy, algorithmic discrimination, transparency, accountability, information manipulation, and cybersecurity. It also examines regulatory responses developed in the United States, China, and Europe, with particular attention to the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. The purpose is to identify the main legal challenges arising from the use of AI systems and to provide elements for reflection on the construction of a regulatory framework aimed at protecting human dignity and human rights in Mexico.

items.title: Intelligent Wearable Systems for Continuous Healthcare Monitoring and Personalized Medicine
items.abstract: Smart textiles integrated with advanced biosignal processing technologies are transforming healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time, and non-invasive monitoring through wearable systems. These wearable platforms continuously acquire and analyze physiological signals such as ECG, EMG, EEG, respiration, body temperature, and blood oxygen saturation. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Edge AI, and machine learning supports on-device signal processing, anomaly detection, predictive diagnostics, and personalized healthcare while reducing latency and energy consumption. This chapter reviews biosignal acquisition, signal conditioning, feature extraction, intelligent processing algorithms, and system integration in smart textile platforms. It also highlights flexible sensing materials, wearable communication technologies, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), and emerging trends such as TinyML, federated learning, digital twins, and self-powered smart textiles for next-generation digital healthcare

items.title: Intent Graph: Navigating the Analytical Reasoning Space for Exploratory Data Analysis
items.abstract: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) is rarely open-ended in practice: analysts work from high-level domain questions toward the concrete analyses that can answer them, prioritizing directions with domain knowledge and prior hypotheses. Large language models (LLMs) can supply such knowledge, but their responses are unstructured, leaving analysts no way to see what has been explored, what is missing, or why one direction was chosen over another. We present DAG-EDA, a system that lets analysts and an LLM co-navigate the space of possible analyses through two linked structures. An intent graph, governed by a grammar of analytical intent, decomposes an ambiguous natural-language question into progressively concrete analysis tasks, keeping alternative framings open and letting analysts branch, backtrack, and compare paths. A multi-layered knowledge graph externalizes the LLM's domain knowledge, linking domain concepts to the dataset variables that can measure them, so analysts can inspect and contest how their question is grounded in the data. Both graphs are constructed from only the dataset and the analyst's question, and the analyses the analyst reaches are rendered as interactive dashboards. We illustrate the system through a usage scenario and describe a user study design for examining whether the system scaffold analysts' reasoning and navigation.

items.abstract: In modern occupational medicine and occupational health, there is a growing interest in studying the phenomenon of occupational polymorbidity. The modern concept of occupational safety is based on the principle that an employee’s health is not an expense, but an investment. This directly aligns with the fundamental principle that health in the workplace and a healthy work environment are among the core values of the individual, society, and the state. However, in practice, implementing this principle faces a serious challenge — the phenomenon of polymorbidity in occupational pathology. items.title: Interpersonal Skills, Leadership Styles, and Team Performance across Key Roles in Indonesian Building Construction Projects
items.abstract: Building construction projects in Indonesia depend on technical competence and funding, but they also depend on the human factors that govern daily coordination among project actors. Poor communication, unbalanced leadership, and weak collaboration are still reported as causes of rework, delay, and interpersonal tension. This study assessed interpersonal skills, leadership styles, and team performance in four stakeholder roles in Indonesian building construction: the team leader of construction management (CM) consultants, the contract signing officer (PPK), the team leader of design consultants, and the contractor's project manager (PM). It also examined how the two human-factor variables relate to team performance. The study used a descriptive mixed-methods design. A five-point Likert questionnaire was given to 26 professionals selected purposively from the four roles; it contained ten interpersonal-skill items, ten leadership-style items, and twelve team-performance items. In-depth interviews with four key informants, one from each role, were analysed thematically. Interpersonal skills were rated high in every role, with mean scores of 4.7 for contractor PMs, 4.4 for PPKs, 4.1 for CM consultant team leaders, and 4.0 for design consultant team leaders. Respondents described leadership that mixed transformational and transactional behaviour, and role means ranged from 3.9 (CM consultant team leaders) to 4.6 (contractor PMs). Team performance scores ran from good (3.7) to very good (4.8) and followed the same order of roles. In the interviews, strong team performance was most often linked to structured communication, conflict resolution based on the contract, and adaptive, participative leadership. Because the three constructs rank the roles in the same order, interpersonal skills and leadership appear to work together as one human-factor system that shapes team performance. Human-factor training in Indonesian building construction should therefore be designed for each role rather than applied uniformly.

items.title: Investigation of ChatGPT-Generated Responses Regarding to Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation in Individuals with Heart Failure
items.abstract: Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the potential of ChatGPT in designing an exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) program for heart failure (HF). Materials and Methods: Two physiotherapists specializing in cardiopulmonary physiotherapy developed 25 questions regarding exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation in HF. ChatGPT-generated responses were evaluated by two cardiopulmonary physiotherapists by comparing them with current clinical guidelines and professional expertise. The relevance, accuracy, clarity, completeness, and consistency criteria for each query were evaluated using a 5-point Likert-type scale. Each criterion's inter-rater agreement was tested using Cohen's Kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis. Results: The two highest means among the evaluation criteria belonged to clarity (mean=4.74, κ =0.78, ICC= 0.74)) and relevance (mean=4.68, κ =0.63, ICC=0.77). The lowest mean and highest consensus belonged to the consistency criteria (mean=3.58, κ =0.93, ICC=0.98). The means for accuracy and completeness were 4.14 and 4.28, respectively. Both criteria had moderate inter-rater agreement (κ =0.40-0.60) and good level ICC (0.75-0.90). Conclusion: ChatGPT directly addressed questions regarding exercise-based CR for HF patients, providing clear replies. However, the responses need to be improved in terms of accuracy, completeness, and, most importantly, consistency. ChatGPT has the potential to support the physiotherapist in the clinical practice. However, as it currently stands, directly using an exercise training program developed by ChatGPT for heart failure patients does not appear to be a reliable approach

items.title: Is In-Domain Training Enough for Fine-Grained Industrial Anomaly Understanding?
items.abstract: A single multimodal large language model (MLLM) struggles to excel simultaneously at detection, localization, description, and reasoning in multimodal industrial anomaly understanding (MM-IAU). We show that in-domain training does not close this gap. On MMAD, a widely adopted MM-IAU benchmark, trained specialists reach at most 75.5% accuracy in defect localization, against 92.3% for human experts, and even detect anomalies less accurately than their untrained base model. Meanwhile, different MLLMs offer complementary strengths but share this weakness in fine-grained perception, so combining them alone cannot remove it. We therefore propose SiGMA, a spatially grounded multi-agent framework that divides labor between heterogeneous MLLM agents and a dedicated visual defect expert. A multimodal searcher supplies industrial knowledge and normal references, the defect expert turns query-reference comparison into calibrated anomaly evidence, and a label-free reliability controller weighs each source by task-wise competence and query-level evidence quality. SiGMA reaches 85.2% average accuracy on MMAD, 4.0% above the strongest trained specialist and Gemini-2.5-Pro and within 1.5% of human experts. Even with three agents of at most 9B parameters, it reaches 84.4%, and new MLLMs join without retraining.

items.title: Is Real-World Training Data Necessary for Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection?
items.abstract: Generalist graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to build a foundation model that detects anomalies on arbitrary unseen graphs without retraining or fine-tuning. Sufficient data are essential for foundation model training, yet generalist GAD still faces a data shortage, as real-world anomalous graphs are scarce and costly to collect and annotate. To fill this gap, we propose AG-FORGE, an Anomalous Graph generation Forge for automatic synthesis of anomalous graphs, exploring the feasibility of synthetic data-driven training for generalist GAD. Empirically, we find that synthetic data can achieve performance comparable to real-world training, but fail to push the performance boundary further due to the limited capacity of existing methods. To further unlock model capacity as training data scale up, we develop TS-GGAD, a Topology-Semantic coordinated Generalist GAD that captures complementary topological and semantic anomaly evidence, together with a curriculum learning strategy tailored to large-scale synthetic training. Extensive experiments on 14 real-world datasets demonstrate that TS-GGAD, trained on data generated by AG-FORGE, significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: Is There a Human Premium in Negotiations? A Relational-Economic Tradeoff in Human vs. AI Bargaining
items.abstract: Abstract Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in large language models (LLMs), increasingly enable AI to serve as an active counterpart in negotiation. Drawing on negotiation theory and mind perception research, this study examines whether attributed counterpart identity, that is, the belief that a negotiation counterpart is human rather than AI, influences relational evaluations, satisfaction, and outcomes in a mixed-motive bargaining context. In a randomized laboratory experiment, 205 participants negotiated apartment rent with the same LLM-based broker but were led to believe the counterpart was either human or AI. After correction across the five Hypothesis 1 comparisons, participants who believed they negotiated with a human reported higher perceived warmth and integrity; perceived competence was higher only in the unadjusted comparison. Participants in the Person condition also reported higher relational satisfaction and agreed to less favorable economic outcomes, paying higher final rents than those who believed they negotiated with AI. Exploratory analyses further suggested that attributed counterpart identity shaped how participants organized and described their post-negotiation experiences, with human-attributed counterparts eliciting more differentiated evaluations and more partnership-oriented descriptions. As AI becomes more common in negotiation, these results highlight the importance of accounting for the relational value people derive from believing they are negotiating with another person.

items.title: Isotope Effects at Classical Cost through Mass-Differentiable Machine Learning
items.abstract: Isotope effects govern fractionation and modulate reactivity, with applications from hydrogen energy to environmental science and catalysis, yet predicting them requires resolving small isotope-dependent free-energy differences that remain very challenging for conventional path-integral simulations in complex systems. Here we introduce iso-EPIGS, a path-integral coarse-graining framework built on a mass-differentiable neural network that reconstructs the mass- and temperature-dependent path integral centroid free-energy surface. Classical molecular dynamics on the learned surface yields rigorous isotope-resolved thermodynamics without explicit path-integral sampling. Benchmarks spanning gas, liquid, and crystalline phases, including liquid water and oxalic acid crystal, reproduce reference path-integral isotope free-energy differences, enthalpies, and lattice parameters at near classical computational cost. Crucially, iso-EPIGS trained solely on all-H and all-D isotopologues retains high accuracy for unseen partially deuterated isotopologues, demonstrating robust transferability across nuclear masses. Iso-EPIGS makes accurate isotope-effect simulations feasible for complex systems and lays the groundwork for foundation models of isotope effects across chemical space.

items.title: Laboratory-based trends in dengue and other arboviruses in the Caribbean: Analysis of surveillance data, 2018-2024
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: To describe laboratory-based patterns of arboviral circulation, including serotype distribution and temporal trends, and their contribution to regional situational awareness in the Caribbean. Methods: This was a retrospective analysis using clinical samples submitted to the Caribbean Public Health Agency Medical Microbiology Laboratory for suspected arboviral infection. Samples were tested using Trioplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunoglobulin M and G enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Data were analyzed by virus type, serotype, age group, sex, and seasonality. Statistical associations were assessed using Pearson’s chi-square tests. Because the dataset is based on submitted samples, findings are presented as proportions among tested samples rather than population-level estimates. Results: Dengue virus (DENV) accounted for the largest proportion of confirmed arboviral infections (34.7%) among tested samples, with DENV-3 as the most frequently detected serotype (65.5%), followed by DENV-2 (26.8%), DENV-1 (4.3%), and DENV-4 (0.17%). Significant associations were observed between serotype and age group (χ² = 201.88; P < 0.001) and sex (χ² = 22.15; P = 0.036). Seasonal peaks were observed primarily between August and November, although an atypical increase in early 2024 was noted. Chikungunya (0.2%) and Zika (0.1%) viruses were infrequently detected. Conclusions: In this retrospective analysis, DENV was the most frequently detected arbovirus among tested samples in the Caribbean, with dynamic serotype distribution and marked seasonal variability. These findings highlight the value of laboratory-based surveillance in strengthening regional situational awareness and informing public health responses, while recognizing limitations related to representativeness and the absence of population denominators.

items.title: Language Modeling is Monotone Compression
items.abstract: A long-standing hypothesis in artificial intelligence and neuroscience posits that intelligence is closely related to compression: the ability to compress information efficiently intuitively reflects capacities associated with intelligence and learning. Indeed, recent experimental works verify this intuition by showing connections between the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and their ability as compressors: for instance, Deletang et al. (ICLR'24) demonstrate that LLMs can be used as powerful compressors, and Huang et al. (COLM'24) show that the compression ability of LLMs is highly correlated with their performance on benchmarks for knowledge and reasoning. In this work, we initiate a theoretical study of this connection. Our main result is that LLMs (formally modeled as next-token predictors) are equivalent to monotone (a.k.a. order-preserving) compression algorithms---namely, compression algorithms where the encoding process preserves the ordering of the inputs---in the sense that the one can be constructed from the other while preserving the same error up to an additive gap of 2. We next show that the monotonicity is required for this equivalence to hold if and only if cryptographic (infinitely-often) one-way functions exist. As a direct corollary, we get a cryptographic result of independent interest: the notion of next-bit pseudoentropy (a computational analogue of entropy) of a distribution is equivalent to monotone incompressibility of the distribution. (Previously, it was only known (Haitner et al., ITCS'23) that incompressibility implies next-bit pseudoentropy.)
